To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

migraine headache is associated with an increase in the amplitude of alpha oscillations, that these changes in alpha power occur at the same rate as the perceived throbbing pain, that the degree of coherence between the two is proportional to the perceived intensity of the headache, that these changes occur at the same frequency as the spontaneous fluctuations in alpha power in the absence of headache, and that they are not associated with changes in heart rate or blood pressure.
the temporal relationship between the throbbing pain of migraine and the pulse of the carotid artery is not one-to-one.

the throbbing pain of migraine is not caused by the pulsatile dilation of vessels, but by a pulsatile modulation of brain activity, in the form of alpha power, that is coherent with the throbbing pain.

the question of how migraine patients perceive their pain, and how the brain generates the percept of migraine pain.
the role of central sensitization in migraine.

migraine pain is not necessarily associated with a change in vessel diameter, although this may be a feature in some patients.

vessels do not play a role in migraine pain.

vessels are not innocent.
migraine is a complex disorder and that a single mechanism cannot account for its many features.
the relationship between the vasculature and migraine pain is complex and not necessarily causal [9].

migraine pain, and its associated symptoms, is not a single entity, and that it is not necessarily the same across individuals [7].
